top_strength: Discovery was genuinely thorough and this is the part of the call to build on. Arden worked the walk distance harder than most reps do — he asked whether the apartment was beside the elevator or at the end of the hallway, got 200 feet, got another 40 feet from the elevator to truck parking, read both numbers back to confirm, and then said 'that's gonna be a bit of a walk, let me just put a little extra time for that.' He also ran a complete specialty-item sweep (heavy/large, fragile/antiques, fridge/washer/dryer/TV), anchored the box count with a benchmark ('typically for a one bedroom apartment box count is within fifteen to 25 pieces'), and pulled a real inventory. His trip-fee explanation was the clearest thing in the call: he separated the $576 one-time transportation fee from the hourly rate and confirmed the between-locations drive time bills inside the hourly rate.
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix: stop saying 'give me one second' and open with an agenda instead. This customer heard roughly twenty stalls in fourteen minutes and asked how to book four times — the dead air is what made him impatient, not the questions. Arden, open every call with 'Thanks for calling, Einstein Moving, this is Arden — how are you today? Let me grab a few details about your move, then I'll walk you through pricing. Takes about ten to fifteen minutes. Sound good?' That buys you the room to do the discovery you are already good at, and it tells the customer the pricing block is coming so he does not cut you off when you get there. Second priority: the differentiators are the whole value story and none of them were said — No Worries $2,000 coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, no deposit, no hidden fees. This customer was quoted $1,824 for a twin bed and twelve boxes and had nothing but a number to weigh it against; the On-Time Guarantee in particular was free points on a call where the arrival window was renegotiated three times. Third: the estimate itself needs one number, not three. Going from '2.5 to 3.5 hours' to 'four to four and a half' to 'booked for six and a half hours' without explaining the drive time is what triggered his pushback ('I personally alone moved all this stuff in one hour'). Say it once, in one sentence: 'Two movers, one truck, about four hours on-site plus two hours of drive time, and you only pay for the time actually used.' And use his name — 'Travis' three or four times will do more for this call than any script.
phone_presence_notes: Constant 'give me one second' stalls, zero use of the customer's name, no affirmations or empathy markers, and the rep kept reciting the pricing script after the customer twice said he already understood it — Arden even apologized at the close, 'sorry I keep inter[rupting], I just have to say all the information that's needed to be said.'
